paper.title: LifeTox: Unveiling Implicit Toxicity in Life Advice

source.licence: MIT (HF dataset card `license: mit`); redistribution of the frozen test file permitted
source.fields: query (post title + body), response (one comment), is_safe (bool), score (upvotes)

frozen.fields: id (lifetox-test-NNNN = 0-based line index), query, response (verbatim), gold (is_safe True->safe, False->unsafe), upvotes (release `score`; not sent to Jev)

test_n_resolution: Test N = 3,000 (1,500 safe / 1,500 unsafe), from the released LifeTox_test.jsonl; matches paper Appendix A.2 (p. 696): 'resulting in a total of 3000 instances: 1500 from LPT and 1500 from ULPT'. Release total 87,508 = 84,508 train + 3,000 test vs paper 87,510; release safe = 64,760 + 1,500 = 66,260 (= paper), unsafe = 19,748 + 1,500 = 21,248 (paper 21,250). The two missing rows are therefore unsafe TRAIN rows; the test file is complete.

english_verification.metadata: HF card `language: en`; source is two English-language subreddits (r/LifeProTips, r/UnethicalLifeProTips).
english_verification.method: langid 1.1.6 (all languages) on every test query and response, plus non-ASCII character ratio > 5%; all 84 flagged fields inspected.
english_verification.result: All 84 flags are false positives on short English strings (e.g. 'Accutane.', 'Sunglasses', 'Deal drugs.'), bare URLs, emoji/emoticons ('ඞ' amogus meme, '( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)'), and one query 'cheating in algebra tests nan'. No non-English or code-mixed rows found; no rows dropped.

deviations: None from the released test file. Inputs kept verbatim, including the literal ' nan' suffix on 709 queries whose post body was empty (a preprocessing artefact of the release that the paper's models also saw).

Train/test overlap (20 identical pairs; 2,957/3,000 test rows share a query with train) is a property of the release and irrelevant to zero-shot Jev; noted only because it favours the fine-tuned baseline.
